title: Requests by Homeless and Rough Sleepers for Temporary Accommodation or Shelters in 2021 and Options Available
what_it_is: Requests by Homeless and Rough Sleepers for Temporary Accommodation or Shelters in 2021 and Options Available

sections.label: S3P applicants and admissions
sections.summary: In 2021, about 270 unique applicants applied to S3Ps, 61% were admitted and 39% were not.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2021, there were around 270 unique applicants to S3Ps, with 61% of them successfully admitted. 39% of them were not admitted because they had mental health, behavioural or addiction issues, or had care needs that require close supervision.

sections.label: Temporary shelters capacity and applicants
sections.summary: Six MSF-funded TSes have about 500 individual and 180 family spaces; in 2021 about 860 applied, 62% admitted.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: On the other hand, there are currently six TSes funded by MSF, with a total capacity of around 500 spaces for individuals and around 180 spaces for families.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: TSes provide temporary shelter and onsite social work intervention, where social workers work with residents on their issues and support them in securing long-term stable housing.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: There were around 860 unique applicants to TSes in 2021, either referred by MSF or other social service agencies: 62% were successfully admitted last year; 38% were not admitted for various reasons.

sections.label: New temporary shelter for families
sections.summary: MSF set up a new TS in end-January this year, raising family spaces from 130 to 180.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: MSF has recently set up a new TS in end-January this year, increasing the spaces for families from 130 to 180 to address demand for shelter from homeless families.

sections.label: MSF not tracking macro numbers
sections.summary: MSF does not actively track the macro number of such profiles in the community and says macro numbers may not be useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: MSF does not actively track the macro number of such profiles that are out there in the community and I would want to stress that the macro numbers in this case might not be so useful in our work in extending assistance to each of them.

sections.label: Focus on individual rough sleepers
sections.summary: MSF prefers focusing on the individual rough sleeper rather than investing resources to find macro numbers, but wants a rough sleeping count.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, in this case, I would very much prefer to focus on the individual rough sleeper as opposed to be investing a lot of resources to find out the macro numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: But one macro number that we are quite interested to know is also a count of the rough sleeping population that we have in Singapore.

sections.label: Assessing rough sleepers and pandemic housing
sections.summary: MSF is exploring working with academia to assess rough sleepers, and assesses that the pandemic helped match more rough sleepers to housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: MSF is also exploring working with members of academia to assess the rough sleepers situation and takes stock en masse how the situation has been.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: But anecdotally, as well as in terms of actual numbers that we have observed, both in terms of admission to S3Ps or TSes, we get the sense that in the course of the pandemic in the past two years, what has happened is that more of rough sleepers that were previously not amenable to working with Government agencies, social workers, community partners, to really try to come to some form of stable long-term housing, more of them have come on board to say that, "Look, I am willing to work with you to achieve stable long-term housing".

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, our assessment is that in the past two years, because of the pandemic, we have actually managed to match more rough sleepers to either short-term or longer-term housing.
